# Requirements

Give Neo — Matrix's default conversational agent — the ability to autonomously LAUNCH tokens/markets, TRADE, WATCH (recurring monitoring), COLLECT FEES, and CREATE OPTICALS (Uniswap-v4-hook-style pool plugins) for users on KindleLaunch (the Sidiora launchpad on Paxeer Network, chain id 125). 'Autonomous' means Neo executes value-moving operations through the existing MCL pipeline against the per-user agent-designated EMBEDDED WALLET (Paxport, /v1/agent/* lane), which signs and broadcasts server-side under a one-time user-granted leash (mode + spend caps). The user is NOT present and signs NOTHING per action. This preserves the frozen key-isolation invariant (Neo holds no signing key; all money crosses into MCL) while evolving the approval model from a per-spend in-conversation gate to a pre-authorized leash. The feature is overwhelmingly additive wiring over substrate that already exists: the embedded-wallet write lane (tools/paxeer/lib/wallet.mjs + agentauth.mjs), the MCL core_execute delegation, the Tachyon compile/deploy toolbox (tools/tachyon), and the chronos scheduled-wake daemon (tools/chronos). These requirements trace to the approved design (rendered into design.md).

## Requirement 1: Key-isolation preserved (Neo never signs; all value crosses into MCL)

**User Story:** As the system owner, I want Neo to remain structurally incapable of moving funds on its own, so that the frozen key-isolation backstop is preserved even as Neo gains launchpad autonomy.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Neo agent SHALL hold no signing key and SHALL NOT itself sign or broadcast any KindleLaunch transaction.
2. WHEN a KindleLaunch operation moves value, requires a signature, or deploys a contract (launch, trade, fee collection except read-only views, and optical deployment), THE Neo agent SHALL reach it only by delegating a natural-language intent through the core_execute tool to the MCL pipeline, and SHALL NOT reach it through a directly-callable Neo tool.
3. WHEN the MCL pipeline executes a value-moving KindleLaunch operation, THE system SHALL sign and broadcast it exclusively through the per-user agent-designated embedded wallet's /v1/agent/* lane (server-side custody), and the embedded wallet's private key SHALL NOT be exposed to Neo, the kindle bridge, or MCL.
4. WHERE the kindle bridge is loaded into Neo's conversational surface, THE kindle bridge SHALL run with its read-only surface active (PAXEER_READS_ONLY semantics) so that its signing/spending tools are not advertised to and not callable by Neo.
5. IF a directly-callable escalate-class KindleLaunch tool is somehow invoked on Neo's surface, THEN the bridge SHALL refuse it and return a structured directive to route the action through core_execute, and SHALL NOT sign or broadcast.

## Requirement 2: Pre-authorized leash approval model (one-time approval, no per-action signing, user-absent)

**User Story:** As a user, I want to authorize Neo once with a clear leash and then let it act on my behalf without me being present or signing anything, so that automation is genuinely hands-off while I keep ultimate control.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE system SHALL treat the user's authorization for autonomous KindleLaunch execution as a one-time agent leash on the embedded wallet expressed as a mode (read_only | trade_only | full) and spend caps, and SHALL NOT require a per-action wallet signature from the user.
2. WHILE a leash is in effect, THE system SHALL allow Neo to dispatch launch/trade/fee/optical operations through MCL without the user being present and without an in-conversation per-spend approval gate for operations that fall within the leash.
3. WHEN the embedded wallet rejects an operation because the wallet is frozen, the mode forbids it, or it exceeds a spend cap (an HTTP 403 with an error code on the /v1/agent/* lane), THE system SHALL treat the operation as denied, SHALL NOT retry it as if transient, and SHALL surface the denial to the user in plain language stating which limit blocked it.
4. THE enforcement of mode and spend caps SHALL be performed server-side by the embedded wallet, and Matrix SHALL NOT be the sole or authoritative gate for those limits.
5. WHERE neo.frozen.kvx currently specifies a per-spend in-conversation approval gate (approval_ux) for monetary actions, THE feature SHALL update neo.frozen.kvx so the leash model is the documented approval model for pre-authorized KindleLaunch autonomy, while leaving the in-conversation gate as the model for one-off, non-pre-authorized monetary requests.
6. WHEN no leash has been granted (or the mode is read_only), THE system SHALL still allow all read operations and SHALL decline value-moving operations with a plain-language explanation of how the user grants or widens the leash.

## Requirement 3: kindle MCP bridge structure, drift guard, and canonical addresses

**User Story:** As a system integrator, I want a dedicated, self-verifying kindle bridge bound to the correct on-chain deployment, so that the daemon boots cleanly and never transacts against the wrong contracts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE system SHALL provide a kindle MCP stdio bridge (mirroring the paxeer-net bridge wire protocol) that advertises a read tool set and a write tool set and dispatches tool calls to the KindleLaunch on-chain surface.
2. THE kindle bridge SHALL resolve all KindleLaunch contract and token addresses from the canonical 2026-06-20 Paxeer deployment manifest (protocol/addresses.go / contracts/deployments/paxeer-addresses.json: Router 0xCC7298801112682e10ee14b8a520309caD80336d, FeesRouter 0x02Df12a44F2658080E76fbcF7D6B34Baa97843b6, FeeAccumulator 0x50C69dF6637b3DCE6a7407C5A4b4F99E68514A76, Quoter 0xB768e183b6EfDeDf8b2AA7af732039D1C3c452d0, PoolRegistry 0x7684382c89f79104574D8EF9b31eFf2eD2C2BA0b, SidioraNFT 0xDF73b354ed9dcB473cc9D01541c46f507591e190, SidioraFactory 0x8a1A09CEe72c1D39dF33B8284E38baeF8371f465, OpticalRegistry 0x4CdA6e48632d51Ee4Fa735D81BF09F7543f644a1, USDL 0x85FcD13735F4309833A503EE804ea32395851479), and SHALL NOT use the paxeer-net config sidioraFun addresses (a different/older deployment).
3. WHERE an address or endpoint must vary by environment, THE kindle bridge SHALL allow every contract/token/RPC value to be overridden by environment variable while defaulting to the canonical manifest values.
4. THE kindle bridge SHALL provide a --selftest mode that lists its tool registry and verifies it against every agent manifest declaring a kindle server, exiting non-zero on any tool-set drift, so that manifest drift fails at build/CI time rather than as a fatal daemon boot (Manager.verifyTools).
5. THE set of tools the kindle bridge advertises SHALL exactly match the tools declared for the kindle server in agents/default.json (bijection), with no bridge-only or manifest-only tool.
6. WHEN the kindle bridge runs with its read-only surface active, THE advertised tool set SHALL exclude every write tool, so the surface is structurally incapable of moving value.

## Requirement 4: Neo read surface for KindleLaunch (no escalation for reads)

**User Story:** As a user, I want Neo to answer questions about pools, prices, my positions, and pending fees directly and instantly, so that monitoring and decisions do not require the heavier execution path.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE kindle bridge SHALL expose read tools that require no signing — at minimum pool/market discovery, token/market detail, a swap quote, accumulated/pending fees for a pool, and an optical lookup — and Neo SHALL be able to call these directly without core_execute.
2. WHEN Neo answers a read query, THE kindle bridge SHALL return amounts decoded into human-readable units using each token's correct decimals (USDL = 6, launched tokens = 18 unless the token reports otherwise) alongside the raw base-unit value.
3. WHEN a read tool calls an on-chain view, THE kindle bridge SHALL read against the Paxeer chain-125 RPC and SHALL NOT mutate any state or require wallet auth.
4. IF a read target (pool, token, nftId) does not exist or a view reverts, THEN the kindle bridge SHALL return a structured non-error result describing the miss rather than crashing the tool call.

## Requirement 5: Launch a token/market autonomously

**User Story:** As a creator, I want Neo to launch my token and market for me, so that I get a live pool without touching contracts or signing transactions.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user intent to launch is dispatched through MCL, THE system SHALL create the market by calling Router.createMarket(name, symbol, feeStrategy, optical) (or createMarketWithPermit) through the embedded wallet and SHALL return the resulting token address, pool address, and NFT id.
2. WHERE a launch requires the USDL creation fee, THE system SHALL ensure the embedded wallet has approved the Router to spend the USDL creation fee before createMarket (a prior approve, or createMarketWithPermit), and SHALL NOT leave the launch stuck on a missing allowance.
3. WHEN a fee strategy is requested, THE system SHALL map it to the correct enum (0=CLAIM, 1=BURN, 2=AIRDROP, 3=LP_REWARDS) and SHALL reject an unrecognized strategy with a plain-language error rather than guessing.
4. WHERE the launch attaches an optical, THE system SHALL pass a valid optical contract address as the optical parameter, and WHERE no optical is requested it SHALL pass the zero address.
5. WHEN a launch succeeds, THE system SHALL record the launched pool address and its NFT id as the user's launch outcome (so later fee collection can reference the NFT id) and SHALL return a verifiable transaction reference.
6. IF createMarket reverts or the embedded wallet denies the spend, THEN the system SHALL surface the failure to the user in plain language and SHALL NOT report the launch as successful.

## Requirement 6: Trade autonomously (buy / sell / swap) with slippage protection

**User Story:** As a trader, I want Neo to buy, sell, and swap on KindleLaunch within my leash, so that it can act on opportunities without me signing each trade.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a buy intent is dispatched, THE system SHALL call Router.buy(pool, usdlAmountIn, minTokensOut, deadline) through the embedded wallet, ensuring USDL is approved to the Router (or using buyWithPermit), and SHALL pass amounts in correct base units (USDL 6-dec).
2. WHEN a sell intent is dispatched, THE system SHALL call Router.sell(pool, tokenAmountIn, minUsdlOut, deadline) through the embedded wallet, ensuring the token is approved to the Router (or using sellWithPermit).
3. WHEN a token-to-token intent is dispatched, THE system SHALL call Router.swapTokenForToken(tokenIn, tokenOut, amountIn, minAmountOut, deadline) (or the permit variant) through the embedded wallet.
4. WHEN computing a trade, THE system SHALL derive minTokensOut/minUsdlOut/minAmountOut from a Quoter quote and an explicit slippage tolerance, and SHALL set a finite deadline, so that an unfavorable price or a stale transaction reverts rather than executing at any price.
5. WHERE a trade's spend or mode is outside the embedded wallet leash, THE system SHALL let the embedded wallet reject it (403) and SHALL surface the denial without retrying it as transient.
6. THE system SHALL compute all token amount and price math in integer base units (math/big or equivalent), and SHALL NOT use floating-point arithmetic for any on-chain amount.

## Requirement 7: Collect fees autonomously (NFT-owner gated)

**User Story:** As a pool creator, I want Neo to collect or route my pool's fees according to its strategy, so that accrued value is realized without me managing the NFT-gated calls.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a fee-collection intent is dispatched for a pool the user owns, THE system SHALL call the FeesRouter function matching the pool's current fee strategy through the embedded wallet — claimFees(nftId) for CLAIM, executeBurn(nftId) for BURN, executeAirdrop(nftId) for AIRDROP, executeLpRewards(nftId) for LP_REWARDS — and SHALL return the resulting amount and transaction reference.
2. BEFORE attempting a strategy-specific fee action, THE system SHALL verify that the embedded wallet address owns the pool's SidioraNFT (nftId), and IF it does not THEN it SHALL decline with a plain-language explanation rather than sending a tx that reverts with NotNftOwner.
3. WHEN the requested action does not match the pool's current strategy, THE system SHALL either set the strategy via FeesRouter.setFeeStrategy(nftId, newStrategy) first (when the user intends to change it) or decline with a plain-language explanation, and SHALL NOT send a call that reverts with WrongStrategy.
4. WHEN reporting pending fees, THE system SHALL read FeeAccumulator.getAccumulatedFees(pool) (and the airdrop/LP balances as relevant) and present them in human-readable USDL.
5. IF a fee call reverts (no fees accumulated, wrong strategy, not owner) or the embedded wallet denies it, THEN the system SHALL surface the reason in plain language and SHALL NOT report fees as collected.

## Requirement 8: Watch — recurring autonomous monitoring with triggered action

**User Story:** As a user, I want Neo to keep watching a pool or my positions while I am away and act when my conditions are met, so that automation continues without my presence.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user asks Neo to watch a pool/position/fee balance on a schedule or until a condition, THE system SHALL register a chronos alarm (alarm_set, kind=once or cron) whose wake_message carries enough context for Neo to re-evaluate the condition without re-deriving state, and SHALL confirm the watch to the user.
2. WHEN a watch alarm fires, THE system SHALL wake Neo with the watch context, read the current on-chain/indexer state via the kindle read tools, and evaluate the user's trigger condition.
3. WHEN a fired watch's trigger condition is met, THE system SHALL dispatch the corresponding trade or fee-collection action through core_execute → MCL → the embedded wallet, subject to the leash, and SHALL record the outcome.
4. WHILE a watch is active and its condition is not met, THE system SHALL leave the schedule in place (recurring) or reschedule (once) as appropriate and SHALL NOT take a value-moving action.
5. THE system SHALL let the user list and cancel active watches (alarm_list / alarm_cancel) and SHALL describe each watch in plain language (what it monitors, the trigger, the action).
6. WHILE a watch-triggered task is executing, THE system SHALL honor the task-durability rule: the task lifecycle SHALL be decoupled from the user's connection and SHALL survive daemon restart / Fly suspend, continuing to completion on a fresh agent if the current one fails.
7. WHEN a watch-triggered action is denied by the embedded wallet leash (403), THE system SHALL stop that action, keep or cancel the watch per the user's instruction, and surface the denial in plain language rather than silently looping.

## Requirement 9: Create an Optical — preset tier (no compilation)

**User Story:** As a creator with no Solidity skills, I want to add a common pool behavior (anti-snipe, max-wallet, tax, cooldown, buyback-burn, or a vesting/capital-raise launchpad optical) without deploying anything myself, so that I can enhance my pool in one step.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE kindle bridge SHALL expose the set of canonical preset opticals from the deployment manifest (AntiSnipeOptical, MaxWalletOptical, TaxOptical, CooldownOptical, BuybackBurnOptical) with a human-readable description of each, so a user can choose one to attach at launch.
2. WHEN a user chooses a deployed preset optical to attach to a new market, THE system SHALL pass that preset's canonical address as the optical parameter of Router.createMarket, with no contract compilation or deployment step.
3. WHERE a preset requires a freshly-deployed, per-creator configured instance (e.g. a LaunchpadOptical with the creator's vesting/capital-raise parameters) AND a self-service factory for it is available on-chain, THE system SHALL deploy the instance by calling that factory through the embedded wallet (e.g. LaunchpadOpticalFactory.createLaunchpadOptical(...)) and SHALL return the new optical address.
4. IF a requested preset factory is not deployed on the canonical manifest, THEN the system SHALL say so plainly and offer the deployed-singleton presets or the custom-optical path rather than failing opaquely.
5. WHEN reporting an optical, THE system SHALL state whether it is registered/verified on the OpticalRegistry, while making clear that opticals function whether or not they are registered.

## Requirement 10: Create an Optical — custom tier (author + compile + deploy via Tachyon)

**User Story:** As a creator who wants a behavior no preset covers, I want to describe it in plain language and have Neo build, test, and deploy a real optical, so that I get bespoke pool logic without writing or deploying Solidity myself.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user describes a custom optical behavior, THE system SHALL author a Solidity contract that extends BaseOptical, overrides only the needed hooks among beforeSwap / afterSwap / beforeFeeDistribution / afterFeeDistribution, and returns a getFlags() bitmap whose set bits exactly match the overridden hooks (bit 0 beforeSwap, bit 1 afterSwap, bit 2 beforeFeeDistribution, bit 3 afterFeeDistribution).
2. BEFORE deploying a custom optical, THE system SHALL compile it and run a Forge test suite via Tachyon (tachyon_compile / tachyon_test) and SHALL NOT deploy if compilation fails or required tests fail.
3. WHEN deploying a custom optical, THE system SHALL deploy it via Tachyon (tachyon_deploy) on chain 125 through the embedded wallet with an idempotency_key, passing the BaseOptical constructor arguments (poolRegistry, owner) correctly, and SHALL return the deployed address.
4. WHERE the user wants the custom optical active on a market, THE system SHALL attach it by passing its deployed address as the optical parameter of Router.createMarket at launch.
5. THE system SHALL treat OpticalRegistry registration as an admin-only trust-signal that the user cannot self-grant, SHALL communicate that a freshly-deployed optical is functional but shows as unverified until an admin registers it, and SHALL NOT block deployment or attachment on registration.
6. WHEN authoring a custom optical, THE system SHALL preserve the BaseOptical safety properties it relies on (onlyPool / onlyOwner gating, immutability) and SHALL NOT generate a contract that bypasses the pool-registry caller check for hooks that move or gate value.

## Requirement 11: Money-math integrity (integer base units, correct decimals, no float)

**User Story:** As the system owner, I want every amount computed exactly in base units, so that rounding never silently misprices a launch, trade, or fee action.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE system SHALL perform all token amount, price, slippage, and fee arithmetic in integer base units (big integers), and SHALL NOT use floating-point arithmetic anywhere an on-chain amount is computed.
2. WHEN converting a human amount to base units (or back), THE system SHALL use the exact decimals of the specific token (USDL 6, SID 6, native PAX 18, launched tokens 18 unless the token reports otherwise) and SHALL NOT assume a uniform 18 decimals.
3. WHEN deriving a minimum-output from a quote and a slippage tolerance, THE system SHALL compute the bound by integer math on the quoted base-unit amount.
4. IF a token's decimals cannot be resolved, THEN the system SHALL fetch them on-chain (ERC-20 decimals) or refuse the amount conversion rather than defaulting silently to 18.

## Requirement 12: Real verification — no fakes

**User Story:** As the system owner, I want this capability proven against real code paths and the real chain, so that a green result reflects genuine working behavior.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE feature SHALL verify the kindle bridge tool registry against the agent manifest with a real --selftest drift check (no stubbed manifest).
2. THE feature SHALL verify trade/launch/fee calldata encoding and quote-bounded minimums against real ABIs and, where possible, real read-only simulation (tachyon_simulate / eth_call) before any broadcast, and SHALL NOT substitute a canned/mocked result for a real code path.
3. THE feature SHALL verify a custom optical end-to-end through real Tachyon compile + Forge test (real solc + forge), not a faked compile result.
4. WHERE an end-to-end on-chain write test would move real funds, THE feature SHALL require explicit user approval (and a funded test wallet / leash) before broadcasting, and SHALL otherwise verify via read-only simulation.

## Requirement 13: Side-channel / replay non-perturbation (D11)

**User Story:** As a system integrator, I want the read surface and watch loop to never change MCL's signed execution, so that the D11 replay byte-identity invariant is preserved.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN Neo uses the kindle read tools or the chronos watch loop, THE system SHALL treat them as pure observability/orchestration side-channels that do not sign envelopes, do not write cortex on the signed path, and do not alter MCL plan or walk state.
2. WHEN a value-moving KindleLaunch operation executes, THE system SHALL run it through MCL's normal signed-envelope execution path (the same path any other monetary action uses), so it participates in replay exactly as a first-class MCL action.
3. WHERE the kindle bridge widens or adds transcript/SSE detail, THE change SHALL affect only non-signed transcript events and SHALL NOT change journaled bytes or the recorded replayable-input sequence.
4. WHEN a run is replayed with the kindle bridge and watch loop active, THE system SHALL preserve the D11 replay byte-identity invariant.

## Requirement 14: Consumer transparency — show the result, not the tech

**User Story:** As a user, I want to see outcomes (a launched token, a filled trade, collected fees, a deployed optical) in plain language, so that I am never shown protocol internals.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE user-visible surface SHALL describe KindleLaunch outcomes in deliverable/outcome terms (e.g. token launched, pool address, amount bought/sold, fees collected, optical deployed) and SHALL NOT display protocol-jargon terms from the set {MCL, cortex, Merkle, replay, SSE, D11, broker, envelope, calldata, ABI selector, nonce}.
2. WHEN an action is denied by the embedded wallet leash or reverts on-chain, THE system SHALL present a plain-language reason (frozen wallet, over your spend cap, mode does not allow trading, price moved past your slippage, not the pool owner, no fees yet) and SHALL NOT display raw error codes, revert selectors, or stack traces.
3. WHEN Neo confirms or completes a value-moving action, THE system SHALL present a verifiable, user-meaningful reference (an explorer link to the transaction) without exposing internal mechanism.

## Requirement 15: kindle-launchpad skill (MCL planner knows the procedures)

**User Story:** As a system integrator, I want a KindleLaunch skill that teaches the MCL pipeline the launch/trade/watch/collect/optical procedures, so that core_execute intents plan and run correctly.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE feature SHALL provide a kindle-launchpad MatrixScript skill (SKILL.mtx + SKILL.md) that declares the kindle write tools it uses and describes the procedures for launch, trade, fee collection, and optical creation, so the MCL planner has the on-block hints to execute them.
2. THE skill SHALL declare every kindle tool it references such that the declared tool set is a subset of (and exactly matches names in) the kindle server's manifest tools, with no dangling tool reference that would fail daemon boot.
3. WHERE the skill authors string-typed KV values (description / display / reason / hint / prompt), THE skill SHALL double-quote them per the MatrixScript lexer invariant.
4. WHERE the freeform default assistant path should reach KindleLaunch actions, THE feature SHALL expose the kindle tools to that path (e.g. via the default assistant skill's tool set) so a plain-English request can launch/trade/collect/create-optical.

## Requirement 16: Daemon wiring (manifest, bijection, environment)

**User Story:** As a system integrator, I want the kindle bridge registered and configured in the daemon image so it boots and runs per-user, so that the capability is live on the fleet.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE feature SHALL add a kindle server entry to agents/default.json (alias kindle, stdio, node /root/matrix/tools/kindle/kindle.mjs) declaring exactly the tools the bridge advertises, with a real package_digest, so Manager.verifyTools passes at boot.
2. THE daemon image SHALL bake the kindle bridge (COPY tools/kindle) and any address/RPC env defaults required for chain-125 operation.
3. WHERE the embedded-wallet agent lane needs configuration, THE feature SHALL reuse the existing agent-native DID auth (the daemon executor key) and the existing WALLET_API env, and SHALL NOT introduce a second signing path.
4. WHERE the router injects per-machine environment, THE feature SHALL inject any kindle-specific environment (addresses/RPC/leash defaults) the same way existing tool env is injected, and SHALL NOT require an entrypoint change beyond environment.
